programs.rate_details: 34% expenditure credit on qualifying UK core expenditure for film and high-end TV. The credit is brought into account as taxable receipt; corporation tax (currently 25%) is deducted, leaving a net benefit of approximately 25.5% of qualifying spend. Animation and children's TV qualify at 39% under the AVEC framework (see separate program entries when added).
programs.minimum_spend_notes: No fixed minimum spend amount. Instead, the program requires that at least 10% of the production's total core expenditure is UK expenditure.
programs.atl_cap_notes: No specific cap on above-the-line spend. Cast and crew wages qualify as UK core expenditure to the extent services are performed in the UK, regardless of the individual's nationality or residence — a key reason the UK is competitive for star-led productions. Qualifying UK expenditure used to compute the credit is capped at 80% of total core expenditure.
programs.qualifying_spend_summary: UK 'core expenditure': expenditure on pre-production, principal photography, and post-production incurred on goods and services used or consumed in the UK. Includes cast/crew wages for services performed in the UK.
programs.non_qualifying_spend: Development costs, financing/legal costs, marketing and distribution, deferments, and expenditure on goods/services not used or consumed in the UK.
programs.application_process: 1) Apply to the BFI Certification Unit for a British cultural certificate (interim during production, final on completion). 2) Production must be made by a UK Film Production Company (FPC) within the corporation tax net. 3) Claim the credit through the FPC's corporation tax return (CT600) with supporting schedules.
programs.payment_timing: Claimed via the FPC's corporation tax return after the end of the accounting period. Payable element of the credit is typically settled by HMRC within a few months of a clean claim; complex claims may take longer.
programs.notes: SEED ENTRY — compiled from program knowledge during initial database build; live re-verification against gov.uk / BFI sources is required before this entry is used for any production budgeting decision. AVEC replaced the previous Film Tax Relief (FTR) regime from 1 January 2024; productions that started principal photography under FTR may still claim under the legacy regime during a transition window — verify which regime applies to a given project.

programs.rate_details: Enhanced rate of 53% expenditure credit on qualifying UK core expenditure for low-budget independent films that satisfy the BFI's IFTC eligibility test. Net benefit after corporation tax is approximately 39.75% of qualifying UK spend. The IFTC operates within the AVEC framework; productions claim either standard AVEC at 34% or IFTC at 53%, not both.
programs.minimum_spend_notes: No fixed minimum spend. Subject to AVEC's general requirement that at least 10% of core expenditure is UK expenditure.
programs.atl_cap_notes: Same ATL treatment as standard AVEC: cast/crew wages for services performed in the UK qualify. The 80%-of-core-expenditure cap on qualifying UK expenditure applies. The £15M figure here is recorded against cap_per_project but is properly a TOTAL BUDGET cap (eligibility ceiling), not a cap on the credit itself — see notes.
programs.qualifying_spend_summary: Same definition of UK core expenditure as standard AVEC.
programs.application_process: 1) Apply to BFI Certification Unit for both a standard British cultural certificate and an IFTC certificate. 2) Production must satisfy the IFTC creative-connection criteria (UK writer or director, or qualifying co-production). 3) Total core expenditure must not exceed £15M. 4) Claim via the FPC's CT600.
programs.notes: SEED ENTRY — verify against gov.uk / BFI before production use. IMPORTANT: cap_per_project=£15M is recorded for query convenience but is actually a TOTAL CORE EXPENDITURE BUDGET CEILING — productions over £15M total core expenditure are ineligible for IFTC entirely; they fall back to the 34% standard AVEC. A downstream estimator must treat this differently from a cap on the credit amount. IFTC commenced April 2024 for expenditure incurred from that date.
